It is a highly liturgical and ritualistic faith, with a strong emphasis on prayer and the performance of certain rituals. In contrast, modern Judaism is more diverse and eclectic, with a greater emphasis on interpretation and innovation. It is more open to influences from other cultures and faiths, and it is more willing to revise and reinterpret Jewish law and tradition. Modern Judaism is also more focused on social justice and human rights, and it is more likely to incorporate elements of other faiths and cultures into its practices and rituals.
